blocks.content: Constitutional bodies derive their authority directly from the Constitution of India, ensuring independence from executive interference.

rows: Mentioned in specific Articles of the Constitution
Created by an Act of Parliament or State Legislature
Established by Cabinet Resolution / Executive Action

items: The Lee Commission (1924) recommended the establishment of the Central Public Service Commission in India.
January 25th is celebrated annually as National Voters' Day to mark the establishment of the Election Commission of India.
Questions frequently test the distinction between Constitutional (e.g., UPSC, CAG), Statutory (e.g., NHRC, SEBI), and Executive bodies (e.g., NITI Aayog).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Constitutional bodies derive their authority and powers directly from the Constitution of India.
The Public Service Commission was initially set up on October 1, 1926, following the recommendations of the Lee Commission in 1924.
The Election Commission of India was formally established on January 25, 1950, a day before India became a Sovereign Republic.
Statutory bodies are created through an Act of Parliament, whereas executive bodies are established via a Cabinet resolution.
